title: Length Reservoir and Compact Prefill Allocator
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Objective: Reduce padding overhead and improve end-to-end latency by introducing a lightweight in-runtime "length reservoir" that aggregates incoming requests into a compact prefill allocator. The allocator forms transient micro-batches with duration and size tuned to amortize kernel startup and attention cost while preserving latency SLOs. This ticket covers design, prototype, and benchmark for the allocator, including kernel selection signals and attention-kernel switching heuristics.
background: We currently observe 12-28% token overhead from sequence padding at our 95th percentile request mix; prefix-heavy workloads and heterogeneous client seqlens amplify wasted compute. Existing bucketizers create many small buckets or force long pads when waiting for batch fill. Our runtime has multiple attention kernels with different per-token cost curves and different memory tradeoffs; selecting kernels at micro-batch boundaries can materially affect tail latency and throughput.
acceptance_criteria: Reduce median padding tokens per request by >= 30% versus current dynamic-bucketer baseline for mixed-length synthetic workload
Maintain P95 latency within 10% of current SLO for interactive (<=300ms) customers under target QPS
Show at least 8% GPU token-cost reduction on production-like eval harness with realistic arrival distribution
Prototype integrated with kernel-cost model and emits diagnostics to /metrics/prefill_allocator/*
implementation_notes: Length reservoir: sliding time-window (configurable 4-20ms) that accepts incoming prefill requests and groups them into candidate micro-batches by a lightweight seqlen histogram
Compact prefill allocator: constructs micro-batches that prioritize minimizing L2 padding while meeting a per-batch amortized kernel cost threshold rather than fixed batch size
Kernel selection signal: compute estimated cost = kernel_startup_cost + per_token_cost * max_seq_len_in_batch; choose kernel that minimizes estimated cost for the batch and respects memory headroom
Attention optimization: switch short-seq streams to tiled MHA kernel; larger max_seq_len batches use chunked-linear or grouped-qkv kernels to reduce memory copy and KV pressure
Prefill priority queue: age-based priority to ensure long-waiting short requests are not starved by continuous burst of long requests (reservoir aging factor configurable)
KV cache reuse: preserve KV cache index mapping across micro-batches when coalesced requests are from same client session to avoid redundant rewinds
Prefill/decode co-scheduling: allow a small decode window to be appended to prefill micro-batch when it is latency-optimal (prefill-then-decode coalesce for short decodes)
Diagnostic emissions: per-batch metadata (chosen_kernel, max_seq_len, padding_tokens_saved, bucket_wait_ms, reservoir_size) sent to metrics. Use tags to correlate with model and hardware.
Backpressure: when reservoir occupancy grows beyond soft limit, fall back to immediate dispatch with conservative kernel selection to preserve latency guarantees

discussion: 2026-02-14 Sofia: Initial design favors time-windowed reservoir vs. count-windowed to better adapt to bursty arrival patterns; suggestion to make window tunable per route.

2026-02-18 Marcus: Prototype shows 22% padding reduction at 10ms reservoir with mixed seqlen distribution; observed small increase in P95 decode latency for one bursty workload - investigating priority aging parameters.
2026-02-25 Priya: Kernel cost curves need per-model calibration; propose offline calibration job that computes kernel_startup_cost and per_token slope for each kernel/model/hardware triple.
2026-03-03 Marcus: Added early stop shipping flag to disable reservoir when memory fragmentation on GPU reported > threshold; avoids OOM risk in worst-case.
2026-03-08 Sofia: Product asked for customer-facing opt-in toggle for aggressive compacting; will expose policy: conservative | balanced | aggressive.
2026-03-10 Marcus: Running 4-hour bench across 4 model sizes; uploading results to drive PR. Observed 9% token-cost reduction on gpt-8b variant when using balanced policy.
decisions: Use time-windowed reservoir by default; make window configurable per route and per customer tier
Kernel selection will be heuristic: choose kernel with lowest estimated cost; if memory headroom insufficient, pick next safe kernel
Expose three allocator policies to customers (conservative/balanced/aggressive) to tradepadding savings vs latency risk
Telemetry fields and tagging schema agreed; include chosen_kernel and padding_tokens_saved as top-level metrics
metrics_baseline: Current dynamic bucketer: median padding tokens/request = 14, P95 latency = 280ms, GPU token cost baseline = 1.00 (normalized)
benchmark_results: 2026-03-09 synthetic-mix-A: reservoir 10ms, balanced policy => median padding tokens 9 (35% reduction), P95 latency 295ms (+5.4%), GPU token-cost 0.92
2026-03-09 synthetic-mix-B: reservoir 6ms, aggressive policy => median padding tokens 7 (50% reduction), P95 latency 340ms (+21%), GPU token-cost 0.86
2026-03-10 prod-like-harness: reservoir 12ms, balanced => token-cost -9%, median pad -31%, P95 latency +8% (still within per-route SLO)
notes: Risk: aggressive compaction can increase P95 for tail-sensitive customers; mitigated by policy knob and canarying
Follow-up: integrate with Optimize recommendations to auto-tune reservoir window per route based on traffic patterns
Consideration: combine with kernel-aware online bucketization for longer-term improvements (separate initiative)
